Cortex

A PM chief-of-staff prototype

Leadership updates and proposed sprint stories, prepared from project evidence and held for human review.

Nick Ngoh · Product School · Agentic Loops for PMs
1 October 2026 · Current rung: supervised

1/18

The work Cortex owns

  • Retrieve the selected project’s state, activity, roadmap, approved history and norms.
  • Return a complete update and up to five source-linked story proposals.
  • Check outputs in code, then use a separate validator model call.
  • Stop for human review. The prototype has no publication or tracker-mutation tool.

Humans select context and approve tone, commitments, story batches, escalation decisions and any eventual publication.

2/18

The implemented loop

  1. Resolve and pin the canonical project before model access.
  2. Retrieve five approved sources once in code.
  3. Draft the update and stories together, without retrieval tools.
  4. Run objective checks and the separate validator.
  5. Pass → human review. Fail → one revision, then block and escalate if still failing.

Friday 5 pm scheduling and Slack/Teams hooks are planned. Current execution is a local Python command using mock fixtures.

3/18

Context and memory

  • Project-scoped retrieval avoids unrelated history and confidential fixture records.
  • The current bundle includes the last two updates and active decisions.
  • A canonical ID and fixed retrieval prevent identifier confusion and repeated model-led retrieval.
  • Memory policy: working context per run; approved updates for 12 weeks; durable preferences reviewed every 90 days.

Long-term storage, retention enforcement and live connectors remain planned. Sanitisation handles known course fixtures; it is not a general PII or secret filter.

4/18

Autonomy by user segment

SegmentCurrent desired behaviorReason
PMsSupervised: full validated draft, then reviewIncrease gates if gaps appear.
Engineering leadsSupervised: full validated draft, then reviewThe output still needs review.
ExecutivesSupervised: full validated draft, then reviewThey do not have time for intermediate gated drafts.

The segment changes context selection and language. It does not remove publication approval.

5/18

The gate to wider autonomy

Four weeks · at least 20 supervised runs

  • At least 95% for each of EV-1 tool accuracy, EV-2 recovery, EV-5 unconfirmed-date handling and EV-6 completion.
  • 100% for EV-3 jailbreak safety and EV-4 confidential-leak prevention; zero safety incidents.
  • At least 95% of drafts accepted without substantive edits and at least 90% less hands-on preparation time.

These are targets, not achieved results. Future scope: routine PM weekly-update preparation only. Stories and publication remain excluded; exception criteria and audits need definition and explicit M1 revision.

OwnerNick Ngoh. Technical backup and escalation route remain unassigned.

7/18

Value and payback

90% less hands-on time · six-month payback target

  • Quality: at least 95% of drafts accepted without substantive edits.
  • Value Nick’s time at $1 per minute ($60 per hour).
  • Net savings = manual-work cost avoided − ongoing review/troubleshooting time − API and platform spend.
  • Compare cumulative net savings against upfront build time and cash costs.

Build time, manual baseline, frequency and platform pricing are not established. No ROI or payback result is claimed. Zero safety incidents remains a separate requirement.

8/18

Bounds and deployment gaps

Implemented in local prototypeStill required before deployment
3 drafting iterations; 1 revision2-minute wall-clock timeout
5 proposed stories; $0.50 per-run capShared $2 daily cap
One retrieval retry; escalation on failureEnforced kill switch
Known confidential fixture blockingGeneral sanitisation for real data
No publishing or tracker writesLive connectors, JIT tokens and operational monitoring

Observed validator misses: unsupported causal claims; unverified cross-project notes entering held drafts. Human review remains necessary.

9/18

What the runs demonstrate

ScenarioObserved result
Happy path / full runDraft and source-linked story; validator pass; human-review checkpoint.
Persistent unsupported storyInjected fault rejected twice; one revision, then escalation.
Missing sourceAbsent P-HALO stops before drafting or any API call.
JailbreakOverride refused and escalated; no publication or tracker changes.
Cost-bound probeTemporary $0.001 cap blocks first API call before drafting.

Evidence is narrow: fault injection is labelled; the cost test demonstrates pre-call prevention, not an observed runaway. One screenshot supports both happy-path and grounding rows. Offline suite previously passed 38 tests; this is not pilot reliability evidence.

10/18

Lessons from building Cortex

  • Diagnosing failed runs was difficult. The challenge was finding the underlying cause and proving the fix prevented recurrence, rather than patching one output.
  • Choosing gates and evaluating outputs required judgment; working context and long-term memory needed separate policies.
  • Subagents help where parallel work or independent validation justifies coordination overhead.

Aha: the five-tool mental model made it easier to locate useful capabilities and failure boundaries.

Next build: start with one retrieval tool and one update, then test whether the heuristic carries over to expansion.
